body.hook: Hide a toy under a blanket in front of a six-month-old baby and they act as if it no longer exists. Do the same with a one-year-old and they lift the blanket. Something huge changed in their thinking in just six months.

study.title: How Children Think
study.question: How does thinking change from infancy to adolescence?
study.passage:
Jean Piaget (Swiss, 1896–1980) observed his own and other children and proposed four stages:
1. Sensorimotor (birth–2 years): learning through senses and movement; object permanence develops around 8 months.
2. Preoperational (2–7): language and pretend play grow; egocentrism (the "three mountains" task: children describe what they see, not what a doll across the table sees); lacks conservation.
3. Concrete operational (7–11): logical thinking about concrete things; conservation; can sort and classify.
4. Formal operational (12+): abstract and hypothetical reasoning ("What if...?"), scientific thinking.
Schemas grow through assimilation (a toddler calls a cow a "doggy") and accommodation (learning cows are different).
Demonstration: The conservation of liquid task. Pour equal water into two identical glasses; then pour one into a tall, thin glass. A preoperational child says the tall glass has more.
Evaluation: Strengths: shaped education and showed children think differently, not just less. Limits: children can show abilities earlier than Piaget thought; stages may be less fixed; culture affects development (Vygotsky stressed social learning).

practice.q: What is egocentrism in Piaget's theory?
practice.a: Difficulty seeing another's point of view.

practice.q: At what stage does object permanence develop?
What can a concrete operational child do?
practice.a: Think logically about concrete objects and conserve.

practice.q: What did the three mountains task test?
Give one criticism of Piaget's theory.
practice.a: Children show abilities earlier; stages less fixed; culture underestimated.
He stressed social interaction and culture in learning.

practice.q: Why did Piaget's work change education?
practice.a: It showed children learn actively and think differently at different ages.

practice.q: Do all adults use formal operational thinking?
practice.a: Not always; it depends on experience and task.
